evaluations.evidence: create a new game
evaluations.rationale: Backlog includes complementary capabilities for games (invite/join, browse/view/export/delete), so game creation is not a missing step and supports feature completeness.

evaluations.evidence: invite estimators by giving them a URL
evaluations.rationale: Complemented by estimator ability to join via URL; invitation is not an orphan capability.

evaluations.evidence: start a round by entering an item
evaluations.rationale: Backlog includes viewing/selecting/re-estimating items and participant estimation behaviors, so starting a round is supported by complementary steps.

evaluations.evidence: see all items we try to estimate this session
evaluations.rationale: Items can be created/added/imported and managed (edit/delete/select), so the list being viewed has a creation source.

evaluations.evidence: select an item to be estimated or re-estimated
evaluations.rationale: Backlog provides ways to create/add items and to re-estimate earlier items, so selection has necessary complementary capabilities.

evaluations.evidence: add an item to the list of items to be estimated
evaluations.rationale: Complemented by view/select/edit/delete of items; item lifecycle is covered.

evaluations.evidence: edit an item in the list
evaluations.rationale: Editing presupposes item creation, which exists (start round/add/import/copy-paste).

evaluations.evidence: delete an item from the list
evaluations.rationale: Deletion presupposes item creation, which is present; item management is feature-complete.

evaluations.evidence: show all estimates immediately
evaluations.rationale: Backlog includes the normal reveal-after-all-estimate behavior and participant estimate submission/change, so early reveal is a complementary variant rather than a missing step.

evaluations.evidence: accept the average of all estimates
evaluations.rationale: Complemented by other ways to finalize an estimate (auto-fill on unanimity, manual entry) and by estimate visibility stories.

evaluations.evidence: estimate field filled in automatically if all estimators show the same card
evaluations.rationale: Supported by estimate reveal/collection and acceptance/entry stories; not missing a necessary complementary capability.

evaluations.evidence: enter the agreed-upon estimate
evaluations.rationale: Complements other acceptance mechanisms and implies estimates exist, which is covered by participant estimation stories.

evaluations.evidence: estimate a story we estimated earlier in the session again
evaluations.rationale: Backlog includes selecting items for (re-)estimation and viewing prior rounds, so re-estimation is supported.

evaluations.evidence: import stories from a spreadsheet
evaluations.rationale: Import is an alternative creation path for items; item viewing/editing/deleting/selecting exists to use imported content.

evaluations.evidence: copy/paste stories from a spreadsheet
evaluations.rationale: Copy/paste is another creation path for items; complementary item management exists.

evaluations.evidence: browse through previous games
evaluations.rationale: Backlog includes game creation and transcript viewing/export/deletion, so browsing previous games has supporting capabilities.

evaluations.evidence: view a transcript of a game
evaluations.rationale: Transcript content is produced by running games (create/invite/join/estimate) and can be exported; no missing prerequisite story is evident.

evaluations.evidence: export a transcript of a game as a HTML file
evaluations.rationale: Export presupposes transcript viewing/availability, which is covered; complementary transcript story exists.

evaluations.evidence: export a transcript of a game as a CSV file
evaluations.rationale: Export presupposes transcript viewing/availability, which is covered; complementary transcript story exists.

evaluations.evidence: delete a game
evaluations.rationale: Deletion presupposes game creation and storage, which is covered; browsing previous games also complements lifecycle.

evaluations.evidence: create an account
evaluations.rationale: Account lifecycle is complemented by login, change details, delete account, and password reminder.

evaluations.evidence: log in using my account name and password
evaluations.rationale: Login is complemented by account creation and password reminder; not missing a necessary prerequisite.

evaluations.evidence: change my account details
evaluations.rationale: Changing details presupposes account creation, which exists; account lifecycle is covered.

evaluations.evidence: delete my account
evaluations.rationale: Deletion presupposes account creation and stored data, which exists; complementary account stories exist.

evaluations.evidence: see dates and times in my local timezone
evaluations.rationale: This is a cross-cutting display capability and does not expose a missing complementary CRUD/flow step in the backlog.

evaluations.evidence: get a password reminder by email
evaluations.rationale: Password reminder is complemented by account creation and login; no missing prerequisite is evident.

evaluations.evidence: select whether to have the team estimate with {…} or {…}
evaluations.rationale: Card-set selection is an optional configuration and does not require an absent complementary capability to make the application feature-complete.

evaluations.evidence: invite up to 15 estimators
evaluations.rationale: This refines invitation capability already present and is complemented by estimator join story.

evaluations.evidence: join a game by entering my name on the page I received the URL for
evaluations.rationale: Joining is complemented by moderator invitation via URL and game creation.

evaluations.evidence: see the item we're estimating
evaluations.rationale: Items are created/added/imported and selected for estimation, so there is no missing prerequisite for displaying the current item.

evaluations.evidence: see all items we will try to estimate this session
evaluations.rationale: Item list exists via creation/add/import and moderator list viewing; participant view is supported by those capabilities.

evaluations.evidence: see that an estimate has been given by a specific estimator
evaluations.rationale: Backlog lacks an explicit story that allows a participant/estimator to actually submit/play an estimate (choose a card). Without estimate entry, showing that an estimate was given is not feature-complete.

evaluations.evidence: be shown all estimates ... after all estimators have given their estimate
evaluations.rationale: Requires the capability for estimators to give/submit an estimate, but no story in the backlog explicitly covers playing/selecting a card to submit an estimate. This missing complementary creation action makes the set incomplete.

evaluations.evidence: change my estimate up until ... all are shown
evaluations.rationale: Changing an estimate presupposes an initial estimate submission capability, which is not explicitly present as a story. The backlog therefore misses a necessary complementary step (submit initial estimate).

evaluations.evidence: see each estimator's prior estimates for the story being estimated
evaluations.rationale: Viewing prior estimates presupposes that estimates can be submitted and stored per estimator per story, but the backlog lacks an explicit estimate-submission story. This exposes a missing complementary capability.

evaluations.evidence: see who gave what estimates during the current round
evaluations.rationale: Requires that participants can submit estimates in a round; the backlog does not explicitly include the estimate entry/play-card capability, so this read/report feature exposes a completeness gap.

evaluations.evidence: start a two-minute countdown timer that all participants can see
evaluations.rationale: Timer functionality is self-contained and complemented by reset behavior; no missing prerequisite capability is implied.

evaluations.evidence: timer reset itself as soon as we all play an estimate
evaluations.rationale: This depends on the capability that participants can 'play an estimate' (submit an estimate), which is not explicitly present as a story. Missing complementary estimate-submission capability makes this incomplete at set level.

evaluations.evidence: scroll back through the stories and estimates from prior rounds
evaluations.rationale: Backlog includes running rounds and transcript viewing; this is a complementary navigation/view feature and does not itself reveal a missing CRUD step beyond the general estimate-submission gap handled elsewhere.

evaluations.evidence: cards in the same order across multiple draws
evaluations.rationale: This is a UI consistency requirement and does not imply a missing complementary capability needed for feature completeness.

evaluations.evidence: change my estimate as long as the draw has not been completed
evaluations.rationale: Changing an estimate requires an initial estimate submission/play action, which is not explicitly covered by any story. This exposes the missing complementary capability.

evaluations.evidence: have a small thumbnail photo displayed near where my cards are played
evaluations.rationale: Displaying a user's thumbnail photo implies a way to provide/upload/set that photo, but no story covers adding or managing participant photos. This missing complementary creation capability makes the set incomplete for this feature.

evaluations.evidence: compliant with XHTML and CSS standards
evaluations.rationale: A non-functional compliance story does not, by itself, expose a missing complementary functional capability required for feature completeness.

evaluations.evidence: have a list of definitions for commonly used terms
evaluations.rationale: This documentation/glossary capability is self-contained and does not imply missing complementary steps elsewhere in the backlog.

evaluations.evidence: created database indexes
evaluations.rationale: This is an internal implementation concern and does not require complementary user-facing CRUD stories to be feature-complete.

evaluations.evidence: function correctly in Internet Explorer 6 and 7, Firefox 1.5 and 2, and Safari 2
evaluations.rationale: Cross-browser support is non-functional and does not expose a missing complementary functional capability.

evaluations.evidence: comply with the W3C accessibility guidelines
evaluations.rationale: Accessibility compliance is non-functional and does not imply missing complementary functional steps in the backlog.

evaluations.evidence: respond quickly to my actions
evaluations.rationale: Performance is non-functional and does not indicate a missing complementary capability needed for feature completeness.

evaluations.evidence: be able to use Unicode
evaluations.rationale: Internationalization support is non-functional/technical and does not expose a missing complementary functional capability.

evaluations.evidence: see sensible and predictable URLs
evaluations.rationale: URL design is a cross-cutting quality attribute and does not imply missing complementary functional steps.

evaluations.evidence: nice error pages when something goes wrong
evaluations.rationale: Error pages are a supporting quality feature and do not require complementary CRUD stories to make the application feature-complete.

evaluations.evidence: results to be stored in a non-identifiable way
evaluations.rationale: Non-identifiable storage implies a complementary capability to access/export/analyze those stored research results in that anonymized form, but the backlog only includes moderator transcript exports (which are likely identifiable by estimator) and a vague metrics story. The research feature set is missing explicit anonymized reporting/export/access requirements.

evaluations.evidence: see some metrics on use of the game
evaluations.rationale: Metrics viewing presupposes that the system captures/records usage events/analytics data, but no story specifies collecting/storing the underlying usage data needed to compute metrics. This exposes a missing complementary data-capture capability.
